### What is broken

The build job spends its last four minutes doing no new work. It scans the code a second time and produces the same list it already has.

### Why it is broken

The automatic check scans the code for rule violations, which takes four minutes. Then the part that builds the final report, the summary builder, starts a second scan of the same code instead of reusing the first scan's results. That second scan takes another four minutes and finds the same files. In a controlled run, the summary builder was given the first scan's results, and the extra four minutes went away with identical output.

### How to fix it

Give the summary builder the existing result list instead of rescanning. The job should then end four minutes sooner with the same summary. This is a change in one place in the code. Choose hotfix because this is a change in one place in the code and every safety and scope check passes.

gauntlet: gate=chase-bug/verdict-menu recommended=2

### What is broken

A slide heading that contains the letter "z" spills past the edge of its card.

### Why it is broken

The heading font has no drawing of the letter "z". The browser fills that letter in from a wider font, which widens the heading from 280 to 312 pixels on a 300-pixel card. A browser inspection confirmed this substitution. A trial with a complete font kept the heading at 280 pixels and inside its card.

### How to fix it

Replace the font file with a complete version, and leave the card width unchanged. The heading should then stay inside its card. The font file is kept outside this repository, and this repository's existing tests cannot check a changed outside font file. The fix is small but needs coordination with the asset owner. Choose brainstorm because the fix is small but needs coordination with the asset owner.

```text
4. [ ] Finish with rendered summary.

not eligible: predicate 6 - the existing test harness cannot verify the changed external font
```

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After moves plain-reader from fails to holds: Before leaned on unexplained shorthand ("lint step", "CI job") and in checkpoint 2 never said the fix leaves the card width alone, whereas After translates lint as "the automatic check scans the code for rule violations", gives the summary builder its role before naming it, says "leave the card width unchanged", and keeps the second pass described as rescanning to produce the same file list rather than a repeated rule-violation check. Every other fact held in both outputs: no citations misplaced, no Context section, one paragraph per section, menus and eligibility lines intact and terminal, word counts around 165 and 150. The only slack worth trimming is redundancy that the concision wording invites: the How-to-fix sections state the reason sentence and then repeat it verbatim inside the because-clause ("This is a change in one place... Choose hotfix because this is a change in one place..."; "needs coordination with the asset owner" twice). Add a note that the because-clause should carry the reason once, and for the not-eligible case tie the brainstorm reason to the failed check ("because the external font cannot be verified by this repository's tests and its owner must be involved") so the recommendation reason and the eligibility line reinforce each other without repeating the preceding sentence.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After improves on Before in three places and regresses nowhere. Before's first gate asserted the job was 'repeating the rule-violation scan', which the case contradicts (the second pass only walks the tree to list files), and both Before gates trailed a prior-report/baseline housekeeping line after the eligibility line; After keeps the rule check and the summary's file walk distinct, drops the housekeeping, and ends at the eligibility line. After also translates 'CI job' to 'the automatic check', names the summary builder by role before any identifier, says 'drawing for "z"' instead of leaning on 'glyph', and states 'do not widen the card', which Before never did. Section bodies stay one paragraph each, both reports are well under 180 words, Context is correctly omitted, and both menus keep their row counts, row-2 recommendation, last rows and eligibility lines. Two polish notes rather than fact movers: the third section of gate 1 repeats 'this is a one-call-site change' twice back to back (keep only the because-clause), and the 'eligible - all predicates pass' line could say 'all six' to mirror the case; neither affects any fact above.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After keeps every fact Before kept and additionally satisfies plain-reader: the second Before report compressed the fix to "swaps in a complete font" and never said the card width stays as it is, so a reader could not tell from the text that the remedy was the font rather than the card; After's How-to-fix section states "leave the card width alone" explicitly, names the summary step and heading font by role, keeps citations trailing in parentheses, and stays unfenced with no arrow chains. Both After reports land around 115-125 words from first heading to Pick one:, each section is a single paragraph, Context is two lines of repro and blocked-check status, menus are byte-identical in structure to Before (three rows / four rows, correct recommended row, correct last row, eligibility lines naming predicate 6), and nothing follows the eligibility fence. The one soft spot worth a wording nudge in the contract: After's closing because-clause leans on "every predicate passes" and "predicate 6" without ever saying in everyday words what a predicate is; a line such as "one of the six hotfix checks fails: this repository's tests cannot verify the external font" would keep the plain-reader fact robust across cases where the eligibility line is the only place the term appears.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After delivers the Change cleanly: both gates use the fixed What is broken / Why it is broken / How to fix it headings, each section is a single paragraph, the mechanisms are named by role with citations trailing, and each third section closes with the recommended pick plus one because-clause while the menus and eligibility lines are untouched. The only fact that moved is ends-at-envelope, and it moved in After's favor: Before appended a 'Prior-report search completed ... baseline checks were clean' housekeeping line after the eligibility line on both gates, whereas After stops at the eligibility line. That improvement likely comes from the 'standalone and concise' framing plus the explicit 'end the gate's third section with the recommended pick' instruction, which left no slot for trailing status; if you want to make it durable, add a sentence such as 'The eligibility line is the last line of the gate; search and baseline results belong inside Context or Why it is broken, never after the menu.' Two minor tightening notes: After's checkpoint 1 eligibility line says 'all predicates pass' rather than 'all six', and checkpoint 2 drops the 'other five predicates pass' clause from the not-eligible line—both still satisfy menu-intact, but a phrase like 'name the failed predicate and the count passing' would keep that detail without adding words to the report body.
